excerpt: Our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) is our voluntary framework for managing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems. It establishes how we identify and evaluate risks, how we make decisions about AI development and deployment, and, from the perspective of the world at large, how we aim to make sure that the benefits of our models exceed their costs.
paraphrase: The RSP is described as a voluntary framework governing risk identification, development/deployment decisions, and ensuring model benefits exceed costs.

excerpt: We have always intended for our RSP to be a living document. We will continually update the RSP as we learn more about AI capabilities and risks, develop and refine technical safety measures, and gain more experience navigating an ecosystem in which the risks to society depend on the actions of many developers.
paraphrase: Anthropic states the RSP is intended as a living document that will be continually updated as understanding grows.

excerpt: The major components of this third iteration are as follows:
paraphrase: This sentence introduces a list of the major components of the third iteration of the RSP.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety outline what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: Industry-wide safety recommendations describe what is needed across the industry to keep catastrophic risks low during rapid AI advances.

excerpt: We lay this out in a table that maps capability thresholds to the mitigations we believe they call for. We also include our planned mitigations as a company, which are drawn from other sections of this policy and associated artifacts.
paraphrase: A table maps capability thresholds to called-for mitigations, and also lists company-specific planned mitigations drawn from elsewhere in the policy.

excerpt: This approach represents a change from our previous RSP, driven by a collective action problem. The overall level of catastrophic risk from AI depends on the actions of multiple AI developers, not just one.
paraphrase: This approach changed from the prior RSP due to a collective action problem, since overall catastrophic risk depends on multiple developers' actions.

excerpt: Our previous RSP committed to implementing mitigations that would reduce our models' absolute risk levels to acceptable levels, without regard to whether other frontier AI developers would do the same.
paraphrase: The previous RSP focused on reducing absolute risk levels regardless of other developers' actions.

excerpt: But from a societal perspective, what matters is the risk to the ecosystem as a whole. If one AI developer paused development to implement safety measures while others moved forward training and deploying AI systems without strong mitigations, that could result in a world that is less safe—the developers with the weakest protections would set the pace, and responsible developers would lose their ability to do safety research and advance the public benefit.
paraphrase: Ecosystem-wide risk matters more than individual risk, since a developer pausing unilaterally could let weaker developers set the pace, reducing overall safety.

excerpt: Although this situation has not yet arisen, it looks likely enough that we want to prepare for it.
paraphrase: Anthropic states it wants to prepare for this scenario even though it has not yet occurred.

excerpt: We now separate our plans as a company—those which we expect to achieve regardless of what any other company does—from our more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.
paraphrase: Anthropic distinguishes its own unilateral company plans from its more ambitious industry-wide recommendations.

excerpt: We aspire to advance the latter through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy. But we cannot commit to following them unilaterally.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to advance industry-wide recommendations via various advocacy means but cannot unilaterally commit to them.

excerpt: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are a new requirement under our RSP. These will describe our concrete plans for making progress across Security, Alignment, Safeguards, and Policy.
paraphrase: Frontier Safety Roadmaps are introduced as a new requirement describing concrete plans across four domains.

excerpt: Goals described in the Roadmaps are intended to be ambitious, yet achievable—providing the kind of forcing function that we consider to be a past success of our RSP.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are meant to be ambitious yet achievable, functioning as a forcing mechanism that has succeeded before.

excerpt: These are not hard commitments but rather public goals against which we will openly grade our progress.
paraphrase: Roadmap goals are public aspirations rather than binding commitments, with progress openly graded.

excerpt: Risk Reports are another new requirement. Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.
paraphrase: Risk Reports are introduced as a new requirement providing detailed safety-profile information at publication time.

excerpt: They will go beyond describing model capabilities, addressing our thinking on how capabilities, threat models (the specific ways that models might pose threats), and active risk mitigations fit together, providing an assessment of the overall level of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will integrate capabilities, threat models, and mitigations into an overall risk assessment, beyond mere capability description.

excerpt: These reports will reflect our reasoning as to whether we believe the risks of training or deploying our models are justified by their corresponding benefits to the world.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will explain the reasoning behind whether training or deployment risks are justified by benefits.

excerpt: They will be published online, with some redactions to protect sensitive details about, for example, our training methods and organizations with whom we work.
paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published online with redactions protecting sensitive details like training methods and partner organizations.

excerpt: As detailed below, we also aim to subject Risk Reports to review by credible, independent external parties.
paraphrase: Anthropic aims to have Risk Reports reviewed by credible independent external parties.

excerpt: Finally, our governance commitments are intended to promote internal and external accountability, similar to those in our previous RSP.
paraphrase: Governance commitments aim to promote accountability, consistent with the prior RSP.

excerpt: Our RSP is only one part of our overall approach to safety. For instance, although this policy focuses on catastrophic risks, they are not the only risks we consider important—our Usage Policy and societal impacts research address other concerns.
paraphrase: The RSP is only part of Anthropic's safety approach, focused on catastrophic risks while other concerns are addressed elsewhere.

excerpt: Further, the RSP may serve some regulatory requirements, but it is not designed to be comprehensive. We want to keep it focused on our most central measures for addressing the catastrophic risks we prioritize most, rather than expand it to address every obligation we face.
paraphrase: The RSP is not meant to comprehensively meet regulatory requirements, but to stay focused on central catastrophic-risk measures.

excerpt: Where regulatory requirements exceed or differ from what the RSP covers, we will address them through separate documents.
paraphrase: Regulatory requirements beyond the RSP's scope will be addressed via separate documents.

excerpt: "Catastrophic risk" as used in our RSP refers generally to risks of the most severe potential harms from advanced AI, such as existential threats or fundamental destabilization of global systems. We use this term in its plain meaning rather than adopting any specific statutory definition.
paraphrase: Footnote 1 defines catastrophic risk in plain meaning terms rather than adopting a statutory definition.

excerpt: Where laws such as California SB 53 define this or similar terms with specific thresholds, we address those requirements in separate compliance frameworks.
paraphrase: Statutory definitions such as California SB 53's are addressed separately in compliance frameworks, not the RSP.

excerpt: This section outlines our recommendations for what it would take, at an industry-wide level, to keep catastrophic risks reliably low through a period of rapid advances in AI capabilities. We lay this out in a three-column table.
paraphrase: Section 1 outlines industry-wide safety recommendations presented in a three-column table.

excerpt: The left column identifies capability thresholds that would call for heightened mitigations. The middle column provides an overview of our planned mitigations, which we have set forth more fully in our Frontier Safety Roadmap and other sections of this policy.
paraphrase: The table's left column lists capability thresholds; the middle column summarizes planned mitigations detailed elsewhere.

excerpt: The right column describes our recommendations for industry-wide safety at each threshold.
paraphrase: The right column of the table gives industry-wide safety recommendations per threshold.

excerpt: The distinction between our plans as a company (middle column) and our industry-wide recommendations (right column) reflects the limitations of any single AI developer's ability to ensure safety across the industry.
paraphrase: The company/industry-wide distinction reflects the limits of one developer's ability to secure industry-wide safety alone.

excerpt: In particular, we cannot unilaterally and unconditionally commit to staying in line with the industry-wide recommendations in the right column. However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot unconditionally commit to the industry-wide recommendations, but they will still shape important company work.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We use these recommendations as the north star for our risk mitigations planning as well as our public policy work. We will strive to advance these recommendations through a mixture of example-setting, addressing unsolved technical problems, advocacy through industry groups, and policy advocacy.
paraphrase: The recommendations guide risk mitigation planning and public policy work, advanced through multiple advocacy channels.

context_stem: However, these recommendations will drive important aspects of our work:
excerpt: We have also adopted a set of competitor-contingent commitments (see Appendix A) aimed at staying in line with these recommendations in scenarios where we can be confident that other relevant AI developers are doing the same.
paraphrase: Anthropic has adopted competitor-contingent commitments to align with the recommendations only when confident peers do likewise.

excerpt: At this point in AI's rapid development, we cannot presently give highly specific advance detail on what evaluations will determine whether risk thresholds have been passed, or what risk mitigations will be needed to achieve safety.
paraphrase: Anthropic cannot yet specify in advance the exact evaluations or mitigations needed given rapid AI development.

excerpt: Our recommendations for industry-wide safety are thus structured around requiring analysis and arguments making a strong case for safety, rather than AI Safety Levels (more in Appendix B).
paraphrase: The recommendations require safety-case arguments rather than fixed AI Safety Levels, detailed further in Appendix B.

excerpt: This leaves flexibility in how risk thresholds are evaluated and how safety is achieved and argued for. But it creates a challenge: one actor's view of what constitutes good risk assessment and mitigation may be very different from another's.
paraphrase: The flexible safety-case approach creates the challenge that different actors may hold very different views of adequate risk assessment.

excerpt: Ultimately, the best way for these recommendations to be implemented is likely via governance of all relevant frontier AI developers by third parties that determine which developers need to provide risk analyses and make arguments for the safety of their systems, and determine which such arguments are adequate.
paraphrase: Implementation is best achieved via third-party governance determining which developers must provide safety arguments and judging their adequacy.

excerpt: To the extent this takes the form of national regulation, different countries should attempt to harmonize their governance, including standards of evidence, to avoid a race to the bottom.
paraphrase: National regulations should be harmonized across countries, including evidentiary standards, to avoid a race to the bottom.

excerpt: In the shorter run, independent bodies (standards-setting organizations, auditors, etc.) might review such arguments and enforce high quality for private AI developers via voluntary mechanisms.
paraphrase: In the near term, independent bodies could review safety arguments and enforce quality via voluntary mechanisms.

excerpt: We expect that the recommendations for industry-wide safety will evolve significantly, as we learn more about AI capabilities, threat models, and risk mitigations. We hope these recommendations will become increasingly specific over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic expects the recommendations to evolve significantly and hopes they become more specific over time.

excerpt: Note that an AI developer might provide a single analysis covering a broad category of models, such that there isn't a new analysis needed for each release.
paraphrase: Footnote 2 notes a single analysis might cover a broad category of models rather than requiring per-release analysis.

excerpt: Additionally, determinations of which AI developers need to provide such analysis should be made with an effort to spare smaller AI developers from unnecessary compliance burden.
paraphrase: Footnote 2 also states smaller developers should be spared unnecessary compliance burden when determining analysis requirements.

excerpt: In particular, at this point AI systems might be responsible for much of the research and analysis that underpins risk assessment, and might have strong capabilities for deception, manipulation and obfuscation of evidence, in which case analyses of threats from AIs should follow very high evidentiary standards with thorough and careful analysis of the possibility that much of the key evidence is suspect due to the possibility of manipulation by AI systems.

paraphrase: Anthropic will maintain a Frontier Safety Roadmap of ambitious yet achievable goals, tracking progress and raising standards over time.

paraphrase: Roadmap maintenance and reporting is part of RSP obligations; it will be shared internally with employees, the Board, and LTBT, and published in redacted form.

excerpt: We will provide updates on whether we achieve the goals, and set new goals when we do.
paraphrase: Anthropic will report on goal achievement and set new goals upon achieving existing ones.

excerpt: Our Frontier Safety Roadmap is subject to change. Some changes may simply reflect our evolving understanding of how best to mitigate key risks.
paraphrase: The Roadmap may change, partly reflecting evolving understanding of risk mitigation.

excerpt: However, we will strive to avoid situations where we revise the goals in a less ambitious direction simply because we are unable to achieve them.
paraphrase: Anthropic will try to avoid weakening goals merely due to inability to achieve them.

excerpt: By establishing this expectation, we hope to create a forcing function for work that would otherwise be challenging to appropriately prioritize and resource, as it requires collaboration (and in some cases sacrifices) from multiple parts of the company and can be at cross-purposes with immediate competitive and commercial priorities.

excerpt: Publishing our Frontier Safety Roadmap may also help inform broader industry and policy discussions on AI safety.

excerpt: Our current Frontier Safety Roadmap is available at anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy/roadmap. We will also keep past Roadmaps available at that link.
paraphrase: The current Roadmap and past versions are published and kept available at a specified URL.

excerpt: We will publish Risk Reports discussing the risks of our systems and how we have made determinations about whether to continue AI development and deployment in light of the risks.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to publishing Risk Reports covering system risks and the reasoning behind development and deployment decisions.

excerpt: These have significant content in common with system cards, but we are adding additional structure and process aimed at presenting our overall assessments of risk.
paraphrase: Risk Reports overlap with system cards but add extra structure and process for presenting overall risk assessments.

paraphrase: Each Risk Report will include all models that are publicly deployed as of its publication date.

excerpt: It will also cover internally deployed models when we determine that these models could pose significant risks above and beyond those posed by our public models.
paraphrase: Internally deployed models will also be covered if they are judged to pose significant risks beyond those of public models.

excerpt: While there are a variety of reasons we might classify an internal model this way, this will—at a minimum—include any internal models that we are deploying for large-scale, fully autonomous research.
paraphrase: At minimum, internal models used for large-scale fully autonomous research will be classified as posing significant risk.

excerpt: Models fitting the above description are abbreviated below as "in-scope models."

excerpt: We may also voluntarily include additional models in a Risk Report, e.g., to contribute to general discourse, but such inclusion does not expand the commitments below.

paraphrase: Risk Reports will be published on a 3-6 month cadence.

excerpt: Note that unlike system cards, Risk Reports will not be published with each new model release.
paraphrase: Unlike system cards, Risk Reports are not tied to individual model releases.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ASL definition changed

paraphrase: The prior ARA threshold was replaced with a checkpoint concept for autonomous AI capabilities.

paraphrase: Reaching the checkpoint prompts further evaluation and accelerated safeguard preparation rather than automatically triggering higher standards.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint
excerpt: We previously considered these capabilities as a trigger for increased safeguards, motivated by an attempt to establish some threshold while we developed a better sense of potential threats.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / ARA threshold now a checkpoint

paraphrase: Anthropic now judges that the initially considered capability levels do not require ASL-3.

paraphrase: A new threshold was added for AI systems capable of significantly advancing AI development.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / AI R&D threshold added

paraphrase: Fixed tests risk missing new risks or being overly cautious relative to the real threshold of concern.

paraphrase: Specific prior methodology figures, such as 1% compute for elicitation or a 6x buffer, were replaced with general requirements to match adversary effort and estimate scaling impacts.

locator: Changelog / RSP v2.0 / Less prescriptive evaluation methodology

paraphrase: Specific methodologies risk becoming outdated as new research emerges.
